The closed button visibly joins both jacket fronts, and the short hem is separated from the complete front trouser waistband by a visible knit strip.

baseline_prompt_en: A photographic study of garment fit centers on a photographed woman wearing clothing with visible fit. The supplied reference guides her visible face and hair: a short dark brown bob with fine separated fringe, dark eyes, softly tapering cheeks and natural rose lips. Her reserved half-smile has the warmth of a small practical success. Keep the independent letterpress-workshop moment at violet dusk. A cream proof sheet hangs by two wooden clips from a drying cord near the old press and type drawers. The woman waits beside it, looking toward the suspended sheet. Her right elbow stays close to her ribs and her bent forearm brings a spare wooden clip to upper-chest height. Her left arm rests down beside her hip, with its relaxed fingers plainly visible. Both feet support her on the wooden floor, one a modest step ahead of the other. The unused clip, printing equipment and hanging paper explain her attentive pause. She wears a charcoal brushed-wool tailored jacket over an ivory ribbed knit, with matching long straight trousers and dark leather loafers. Each sleeve is set into the jacket at the shoulder edge. The top of each sleeve cap has a thin raised wool rim, immediately above a separately readable recessed attachment seam. The raised rim and the seam below it form two distinct shallow edges of that same sleeve-to-jacket join. The rim is made from the jacket wool and follows the curved sleeve cap. Grazing light and a small contact shadow between these edges reveal their physical height difference. One central button and its corresponding buttonhole visibly connect the two jacket fronts just above the short lower hem. The fastened front has room around her torso, with a few gentle hanging folds. The jacket lower edge finishes a few centimeters above the trouser waistband all across the front. A horizontal strip of ivory knit visibly separates that jacket hem from the complete front waistband, including its left and right ends. The trouser band follows the natural waist, while the same trousers hang freely through the thighs and knees. Their long straight legs end over the loafer insteps in a small soft break, with the hems raised above the floor. Cool window light grazes the sleeve-cap rims and the jacket lower edge so their adjoining seams and gap remain readable. Amber task light continues to warm her left cheek and the spare clip. The dry wool texture, knit ribs, matte cream paper and worn floor retain their distinct surfaces within the same room. Use the same calm full-length vertical portrait, from hair to both soles with breathing room, in a three-quarter frontal view at lower-chest camera height. The press and paper remain beside and behind her. Her face leads the viewer into the waiting moment, and the jacket join, fastener, waist gap and trouser-to-shoe continuity remain large enough to inspect within the environmental portrait.
